title: Removing the entry after a literal block scalar whose last line starts with a hash takes only the comment above the entry
notes: The literal scalar of `a` has two lines, `x` and `# in`, both indented two spaces. A line of a block scalar is content (production 170, l-literal-content), whatever it starts with, so `  # in` is part of the text, not a comment: the value is `x\n# in\n`. The line `# h` is at column 0, which ends the scalar, and is a comment directly above the entry `b`. Removing `/b` takes the entry and, by the kit's convention for comments (docs/edit-semantics.md: a comment on the line directly above an entry, with no blank line between, goes with it), that comment; the specification gives comments no owner, so the case carries the tags `convention` and `comment-ownership`. The scalar of `a`, with `  # in`, is not touched and `c: 2` stays: a library that takes `  # in` for the comment above `b`, or that stops the scalar early, removes a line that is data.

provenance.reference: A patch engine that took the hash lines at the end of a block scalar for the comments above the next entry and removed them with it, or kept the comment that belongs to the removed entry.
